items.text: An atom of xenon has eight electrons in its outermost energy level, and each fluorine atom uses one of its electrons to form a covalent bond. The outer energy shell now contains 12 electrons. These are arranged insixpairs,forming anoctahedral arrangement.Twoofthesepairs arelonepairs,which repel eachother and are thereforelocated opposite each otherSo,thefourbonding pairs are in a plane, with the four fuorine atoms at the corners of a square and an F-Xe-F bond angle of 90°,as shown in fig A.
